Class IdeHandle

java.lang.Object
uno.anahata.asi.agi.resource.handle.ResourceHandle
uno.anahata.asi.ide.resources.handle.IdeHandle
All Implemented Interfaces:
Rebindable
public abstract class IdeHandle extends ResourceHandle implements Rebindable
Universal abstract base class for IDE-integrated resource handles.

Bridges host IDE Virtual File Systems (such as NetBeans FileObject and IntelliJ VirtualFile) to the Anahata resource pipeline. Manages URI normalization, absolute filesystem paths, existence checks, unsaved editor state detection (isModified()), and contextual prompt augmentation via getAnnex().

VCS and Local History Integration: Dynamically queries the session's active AbstractVCS toolkit to supply live working-copy diffs and chronological history snapshots directly to the prompt annex without coupling the core framework.

Author:
anahata

    • isVirtual

      public boolean isVirtual()
      Determines if this is a virtual, memory-backed handle.

      High-Fidelity Strategy: Virtual handles (snippets) typically trigger the 'Preview-as-Editor' mode in viewers to ensure constant IDE fidelity without card-swapping.

      IDE handles always represent persistent physical or VFS resources, not memory-backed snippets.

      Specified by:
      isVirtual in class ResourceHandle
      Returns:
      true if virtual (in-memory content).

    • write

      public abstract void write(String content, String reason) throws IOException
      Agnostically writes text content back to the resource with a descriptive reason.

      Purity Note: Read-only handles should throw UnsupportedOperationException.

      Persists content changes through the host IDE's editor or filesystem APIs while labeling Local History snapshots with the provided reason.

      Overrides:
      write in class ResourceHandle
      Parameters:
      content - The text to write.
      reason - The reason or explanation for this modification, used for version control or local history labels.
      Throws:
      IOException - if the write fails.
